mainTopic: The two readings of the משנה, the sources for excluding אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו and a maternal brother from יבום, and the argument of רב and רב יהודה about זיקה
overview: The גמרא first settles a disagreement about the wording of the משנה: some call the woman who must leave 'the first' and others call her 'the second.' Both readings are shown to be correct. 'First' means first to fall to יבום, and 'second' means she has been married twice. Next, רב learns from 'כי ישבו אחים יחדו' that there is no יבום with אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו. From 'יחדו' he also learns that a brother from the mother only is excluded. רבה learns that second rule instead from a גזירה שוה of 'אחים' by the sons of יעקב. The גמרא explains why that source beats עריות and לוט, and why the תורה needed both 'אחים' and 'יחדו'. Then רב (quoted by רב הונא) says that if a שומרת יבם dies, the יבם may marry her mother, because אין זיקה, and the גמרא explains his exact wording and defends him from a משנה. Finally, רב יהודה forbids the mother because יש זיקה, and the גמרא begins explaining his wording, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The reading 'first' means first to fall to יבום
steps.stepSummary: The one who reads the משנה as 'the first' wife is correct. 'First' means she was the first to fall before the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches 'the first' is not mistaken. What does 'first' mean? The first to fall to יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the reading of the משנה that calls the יבמה 'the first.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the wife of the first brother who died is the one who must leave. She can be called 'first' because she was the first woman to fall to יבום. Calling her 'first' is about the order of falling to יבום, not the order of anything else.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who teaches (a version of the text)
Falling: when a widow becomes bound to her husband's brother for יבום

phrases.english: [The one who teaches] 'the first' is not mistaken,
phrases.notes: The words 'the one who teaches' (מאן דתני) come right before this line in the גמרא.

phrases.english: What does 'first' mean?
The first to fall [to יבום].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by defending the first version of the משנה's text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word so the reading makes sense
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ראשונה' means first to fall to יבום.

steps.title: The reading 'second' means second to marry him
steps.stepSummary: The one who reads 'the second' is also correct. 'Second' means she was the second wife the brother married.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who teaches 'the second' is not mistaken either. What does 'second' mean? Second in the order of marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now defends the other reading of the משנה, which calls the same woman 'the second.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second brother was already married to his own wife. When he did יבום with his dead brother's wife, she became his second wife. So she is 'second' in the order of his marriages.

phrases.english: And the one who teaches 'the second' is not mistaken,
What does 'second' mean?
Second to be married [to the brother who did יבום].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 1 by defending the second version of the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word so the reading makes sense
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two readings seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Second' can mean second in the order of marriages.

steps.title: But what if he did יבום first and married the other wife later?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that explanation. The case could also happen when the brother did יבום first and only afterward married another wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Aren't we also dealing with a case where he did יבום first and then afterward married another wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from step 2, that 'second' means second to marry him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דין of the משנה should be the same even if the brother did יבום first and married his other wife later. In that case the יבמה would be his first wife, not his second. So 'second to marry' cannot be a reliable way to describe her.

keyTerms.meaning: Aren't we (also) dealing with…? A challenge showing a case the explanation does not cover
He did יבום (married his dead brother's widow)

phrases.english: Aren't we [also] dealing with
a case where he did יבום and only afterward married [another wife]?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּיִבֵּם וְאַחַר כָּךְ כָּנַס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of 'second' given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that 'שניה' means second to marry the brother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's דין also applies when the יבום happened first. In that case she is his first wife, so the explanation does not cover every case.

steps.title: 'Second' means she has been married twice
steps.stepSummary: The new explanation: she is 'second' because this is her own second marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'second' mean? Second in marriage: she is married for the second time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old explanation and gives a new one that works in every order of events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'second' describes the woman herself, not the brother's order of marriages. The יבמה was married once to her first husband and again to the יבם, so she has been married twice. This is true no matter which wife the brother married first.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: introduces a new explanation that replaces the old one
Second in marriage: married for a second time

steps.whatToRemember: Both readings of the משנה are correct. 'First' means first to fall to יבום, and 'second' means this woman has been married twice.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the small change from לְנִשּׂוּאִין (step 2) to בְּנִשּׂוּאִין (here). The first means second in the brother's order of marriages. The second means it is her own second marriage.

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'second' mean?
Second in marriage [she is married for the second time].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by replacing the explanation from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the earlier explanation with a better one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Second' meant second to marry the brother.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Second' means the woman herself has been married twice.

steps.title: Where does the תורה teach אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the פסוק that excludes the wife of a brother who was never alive at the same time as you.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is it written that the wife of a brother who was not in the world with him [is excluded from יבום]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the wording of the משנה to the source of its main law. It asks where the תורה teaches this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that a brother born after his brother died has no יבום with that brother's wife. The גמרא wants a פסוק as the basis for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of a brother who was not alive at the same time as him

phrases.english: The wife of his brother who was not in the world with him:
where is it written?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ הֵיכָא כְּתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: from the wording of the משנה to the פסוק behind its law.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that excludes אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו from יבום.

steps.title: רב: 'כי ישבו אחים יחדו' means they lived at the same time
steps.stepSummary: רב learns from 'when brothers dwell together' that the brothers must have been alive at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The פסוק says 'When brothers dwell together.' This means they shared one time of living in the world. That excludes the wife of a brother who was not in the world with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Dwelling together' is read as being alive in the world at the same time. A brother born after the other one died never 'dwelled together' with him. So the law of יבום does not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: One shared time of living in the world

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the whole case of the משנה. It explains why the first brother's wife (the ראשונה) is exempt as אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו; the other wife leaves only because she is her צרה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The verse says:
'When brothers dwell together,'
meaning that they had one shared dwelling in the world,

phrases.aramaic: פְּרָט לְאֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ.
phrases.english: which excludes the wife of his brother who was not in the world with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כי ישבו אחים' means they lived in the world at the same time.

steps.title: 'יחדו' excludes a brother from the mother only
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק's word 'together' teaches that the brothers must share an inheritance. That leaves out a brother from the mother only.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Together' means joined in inheritance. That excludes his brother from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רב learns a second rule from the word 'יחדו': יבום applies only to brothers from the same father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheritance passes through the father. Only brothers with the same father are 'joined' in inheritance. So a brother from the mother only (אח מן האם) is not included in יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: His brother from the mother only (a half-brother)

phrases.english: 'Together': joined in inheritance,
phrases.notes: Only sons of the same father inherit together, since inheritance passes through the father.

phrases.english: which excludes his brother from the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's teaching with a second lesson from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יבום applies only to brothers from the same father, not to a brother from the mother only.

steps.title: רבה: learn 'brothers from the father' from the sons of יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a different source: a גזירה שוה from the brothers in the story of יעקב's sons, who shared a father but not a mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The rule that it means brothers from the father is learned from the word 'brotherhood' here and 'brotherhood' by the sons of יעקב. There, they were brothers from the father and not from the mother. So too here, it means from the father and not from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers another way to prove that יבום applies only to brothers from the same father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word for brothers appears both by יבום and by the sons of יעקב. The sons of יעקב had four different mothers but one father. So the word 'brothers' in the יבום פסוק also means brothers from the father.

keyTerms.meaning: Brotherhood (the word for brothers), used here for a גזירה שוה
Just as there… so too here: the pattern of a comparison

phrases.english: Rabba said:
[That it means] brothers from the father, he learns
from 'brotherhood' and 'brotherhood' of the sons of Yaakov:

phrases.aramaic: מַה לְהַלָּן — מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: just as there, it is from the father and not from the mother,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן — מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: so too here, it is from the father and not from the mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: אַחִין מִן הָאָב יָלֵיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source than רב's 'מיוחדים בנחלה' for excluding a brother from the mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גזירה שוה from the sons of יעקב teaches that יבום applies only to brothers from the father.

steps.title: Why not learn 'brothers' from עריות instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't compare to the laws of עריות, where a brother from the mother also counts as a brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn 'brotherhood' and 'brotherhood' from עריות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's גזירה שוה by suggesting a different comparison that would give the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of עריות, a brother's wife is forbidden even if he is a brother from the mother only. If we compared to עריות, a brother from the mother would be included in יבום. So why choose the sons of יעקב over עריות?

keyTerms.meaning: But let us learn (a challenge offering another source)

phrases.english: But let him learn 'brotherhood' and 'brotherhood' from the forbidden relationships!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's choice of comparison in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's גזירה שוה from the sons of יעקב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another comparison exists, to עריות, where a brother from the mother counts. It would lead to the opposite result, so why prefer the sons of יעקב?

steps.title: Learn 'אחים' from 'אחים', not from 'אחיך'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the sons of יעקב use the same word 'אחים' as the יבום פסוק, while עריות says 'אחיך', so that comparison is weaker.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'brothers' from 'brothers.' We do not learn 'brothers' from 'your brother.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by explaining why the comparison to the sons of יעקב is the better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה works best when the words match exactly. The יבום פסוק and the story of יעקב's sons both say 'אחים' (brothers). The עריות פסוק says 'אחיך' (your brother), which is a weaker match.

keyTerms.meaning: Your brother: the wording used by עריות

steps.whatToRemember: There is no יבום for a brother born after his brother died (from 'ישבו… יחדו'). There is also no יבום for a brother from the mother only. רב learns that from 'יחדו', and רבה from 'אחים' of the sons of יעקב, which matches better than 'אחיך' of עריות.

phrases.english: We learn 'brothers' from 'brothers,'
and we do not learn 'brothers' from 'your brother.'
phrases.notes: The עריות פסוק speaks of 'your brother's wife', a different form of the word than 'brothers.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Preferring the comparison whose wording matches exactly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps יבום should be compared to עריות, which would include a brother from the mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אחים' matches 'אחים' of the sons of יעקב better than 'אחיך' of עריות, so רבה's comparison stands.

steps.title: Why should a small difference in wording matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous answer. רבי ישמעאל's school made a גזירה שוה between 'ושב' and 'ובא', two completely different words. So why should the small difference between 'אחים' and 'אחיך' stop us from comparing to עריות?
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does that make? Didn't the school of רבי ישמעאל compare 'and the כהן shall return' with 'and the כהן shall come', saying returning and coming are the same thing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 10's answer. If two totally different words can be compared, then 'אחים' and 'אחיך' should surely be close enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said עריות is a weaker match because it says 'אחיך' and not 'אחים'. But רבי ישמעאל's school linked 'שיבה' (returning) and 'ביאה' (coming), which are not even the same word. If that kind of link works, a one-letter difference shouldn't matter, and we should learn from עריות after all.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל
Returning (of the כהן to check the house)

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
But the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
"And the kohen shall return," "And the kohen shall come,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:39 and 14:44, about a house with צרעת.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה!
phrases.english: returning is the same as coming!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ, הָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 10's claim that 'אחיך' and 'אחים' are too different for a strong גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even different words like שיבה and ביאה can be compared, a one-letter difference should not block the comparison to עריות.

steps.title: When a closer match exists, we learn from the closer match
steps.stepSummary: The rule of רבי ישמעאל's school only applies when there is nothing more similar. Here, the sons of יעקב use the exact word 'אחים', so we learn from them and not from עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: That only applies where there is nothing more similar. But where there is something more similar, we learn from the more similar one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: comparing different-looking words is fine, but only when no closer match is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that 'אחיך' could, in principle, be compared to 'אחים'. But the sons of יעקב use the very same word 'אחים', which is a better match. When there is a choice, the closest match wins.
steps.whatToRemember: A גזירה שוה can link words that look different, but if a closer match exists, we learn from the closer one.

phrases.english: That applies where
there is nothing more similar to it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ
phrases.english: but where there is something more similar,
we learn from what is more similar to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the earlier principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any similar-enough word is as good as any other for a גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: When an exact match exists (בני יעקב, 'אחים'), we prefer it over a looser match (עריות, 'אחיך').

steps.title: Why not learn 'brothers' from לוט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another source: אברהם called himself and לוט 'brothers', even though they were only relatives. Why not learn from there?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn 'brothers' from 'brothers' in the story of לוט, as it is written: 'For we are men who are brothers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different פסוק with the exact word 'אחים' and asks why we don't learn from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אחים' is used for לוט with the same exact word, so the closest-match rule from step 12 doesn't help. If we learned from לוט, 'brothers' could mean any close relatives, and that would change who counts for יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Brotherhood (the word 'brothers' used as the link)

phrases.english: But let us learn "brothers" from "brothers" from לוט,
as it is written: "For we are men who are brothers!"
phrases.notes: בראשית 13:8. אברהם is speaking to לוט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New challenge to רבה's source, after step 12's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's choice of the sons of יעקב as the source (step 8)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לוט also uses the exact word 'אחים', so it is just as close a match and should be just as good a source.

steps.title: The word 'brothers' by יעקב's sons is extra, so it is a better source
steps.stepSummary: It makes more sense to learn from the sons of יעקב, because there the word 'אחים' is extra (מופנה). The פסוק could have said 'sons of our father' and still chose 'brothers', so the word is free to teach something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes more sense to learn from the sons of יעקב, because the word there is 'free'. Since the פסוק could have written 'We your servants are twelve sons of our father', and it wrote 'brothers' instead, learn from this that the word is there to be free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the sons of יעקב are a stronger source than לוט: their 'אחים' is an extra word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה is stronger when the linking word is not needed in its own story. The brothers could have called themselves 'sons of our father'; using 'אחים' instead shows the word is extra. That extra word is meant to teach elsewhere, here about יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Free, extra; a word not needed in its own context, so it can be used to teach elsewhere

steps.confusionAlert: 'Free' does not mean the word is meaningless. It means the פסוק could have said the same thing another way, so the choice of this word is extra and available to teach a lesson.

phrases.english: It is more reasonable that from the sons of יעקב
one should learn,
because it is "free":
since it could have written
"We your servants are twelve sons of our father,"
phrases.notes: This is how the פסוק could have been worded. The real פסוק is בראשית 42:13.

phrases.english: and instead "brothers" is written,
learn from it that it is there to be free.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף, מִשּׁוּם דְּמַפְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that one source is stronger because its word is extra (מופנה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוט and the sons of יעקב are equally good sources, since both say 'אחים'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sons of יעקב are better, because their 'אחים' is extra and therefore available for a גזירה שוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key rule of גזירה שוה: a word that is extra in its own setting is a stronger link.

steps.title: Both 'אחים' and 'יחדו' had to be written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the יבום פסוק needed both words: 'אחים' and 'יחדו'. Next it will explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write 'brothers', and it was necessary to write 'together'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it says both words are needed and is about to explain why each one matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 learned the rule from 'יחדו', and step 8 learned it from 'אחים'. So it looks like one word would be enough. The גמרא says both words are needed and will explain each one.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "brothers,"
and it was necessary to write "together."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבה's source to explaining why both words appear in the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both 'אחים' and 'יחדו' are needed in the יבום פסוק.

steps.title: Without 'יחדו', we might have learned from לוט
steps.stepSummary: If only 'אחים' were written, we might have learned from לוט, where 'אחים' is also extra, since the פסוק could have said 'friends'. That would make even relatives count. So the תורה wrote 'יחדו': only brothers who share an inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written only 'brothers', I would have said: learn 'brothers' from לוט. And if you say that word is not free, not so, it is free, since it could have written 'friends' and wrote 'brothers' instead. So the תורה wrote 'together': those united in inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why 'אחים' alone is not enough. We could have learned from לוט instead of from the sons of יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said לוט is weaker because its word isn't extra. Here the גמרא says it really is extra, since 'רעים' (friends) could have been used. So without 'יחדו', learning from לוט would be possible, and 'יחדו' rules it out by requiring a shared inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: Those united in inheritance (sharing a father)

phrases.english: For if the Merciful One had written only "brothers,"
I would have said:
learn "brothers" from "brothers" from לוט,
and if you say it is not free,
phrases.notes: This is the answer the גמרא gave in step 14, and now it is being questioned.

phrases.english: not so, it is indeed free,
since it could have written "friends,"
and "brothers" is written,
learn from it that it is there to be free.
So the Merciful One wrote "together,"
meaning those who are united in inheritance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of step 15: why 'יחדו' is needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'יחדו' is needed to block learning from לוט, limiting יבום to brothers who share an inheritance (from the father).

steps.title: Without 'אחים', we might require the same father and mother
steps.stepSummary: If only 'יחדו' were written, we might think the brothers must share both father and mother. 'אחים' teaches, through the sons of יעקב, that sharing a father is enough. So both words are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only 'together', I would have said they must share both father and mother. So both words are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation. Each word blocks a different mistake, so both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יחדו' alone might mean fully united, sharing both parents. 'אחים' links to the sons of יעקב, who had one father and different mothers, and shows that a shared father is enough. Together, the two words give the exact rule.
steps.whatToRemember: 'יחדו' rules out loose relatives like לוט, and 'אחים' shows that a shared father is enough, like the sons of יעקב. Together: יבום applies to brothers from the same father.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only "together,"
I would have said
that they must be united in both father and mother,
so both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation begun in step 15, giving the reason 'אחים' is needed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both words are needed: 'יחדו' limits יבום to brothers who share an inheritance, and 'אחים' (from the sons of יעקב) shows that a shared father, without a shared mother, is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule of יבום: a brother from the same father counts, while a brother from the mother only, or a more distant relative, does not.

steps.title: Why would we think a shared mother matters?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 17 that, without the word 'אחים', we might require brothers from both the same father and the same mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where would that idea even come from? The תורה ties יבום to inheritance, and inheritance comes from the father, not the mother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the last point: why would anyone think יבום needs brothers who share a mother too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבם takes his brother's place and inherits from him, so יבום is linked to נחלה. Since brothers only inherit from each other through the father, the mother should not matter at all. So it seems we never needed 'אחים' to teach that sharing a father is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: From where would it come? (Why would we think this?)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: But this, from where would it come?
phrases.notes: 'This' means the idea from step 17, that the brothers might need to share a mother too.

phrases.english: The Merciful One made יבום depend on inheritance,

phrases.aramaic: וְנַחֲלָה מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם הִיא!
phrases.english: and inheritance comes from the father and not from the mother!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 17 for why 'אחים' is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that without 'אחים' we would require brothers sharing both father and mother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יבום depends on inheritance, which only comes through the father, so the mother was never relevant and 'אחים' seems unnecessary for this.

steps.title: Because יבום permits a forbidden relation, we might have limited it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that since יבום is a חידוש that permits a brother's wife, we might have limited it to full brothers. So the word 'אחים' is still needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since it is a special new rule that a forbidden woman becomes permitted to him, say it only applies when the brothers share both a father and a mother. That is why it was necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 17: the word 'אחים' really is needed, because of a different reason to limit יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother's wife is normally an ערוה. Because יבום permits her, it is a חידוש, and a חידוש is usually read narrowly, so we might have limited it to full brothers. The word 'אחים', learned from the sons of יעקב, shows that sharing a father is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind to say
A special new rule that goes against the normal law

steps.whatToRemember: Both 'אחים' and 'יחדו' are needed: 'יחדו' excludes mere relatives, and 'אחים' shows that brothers from the same father are enough, even though יבום is a חידוש.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
it could enter your mind to say:
since it is a novelty
that a forbidden relation becomes permitted to him,
say it applies only when they share a father and a mother,
so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 and keeps step 17's conclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason for the הוה אמינא (חידוש is read narrowly)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since יבום permits an ערוה, it might be limited to brothers from the same father and the same mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אחים' teaches that brothers from the same father are enough, even though יבום is a חידוש.

steps.title: If the waiting widow dies, the יבם may marry her mother
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רב: if a שומרת יבם dies, the יבם is allowed to marry her mother. The גמרא concludes that רב holds אין זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: A woman waiting for her יבם who died, he is permitted to marry her mother. So רב must hold that there is no זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling of רב, and draws out the opinion behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife's mother is forbidden to a man. If the bond (זיקה) between the יבם and the widow made her like his wife, her mother would be forbidden to him. Since רב permits the mother, he must hold that the bond does not create that kind of connection.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her husband's brother to do יבום or חליצה
He is permitted to marry her mother
The bond between the widow and the יבם before יבום

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
a woman waiting for her yavam who died,
he is permitted to marry her mother,
evidently he holds there is no zikah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם שֶׁמֵּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of 'אחים' and 'יחדו' ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a שומרת יבם dies, the יבם may marry her mother, which shows רב holds אין זיקה.

steps.title: Why not just rule like the opinion that there is no זיקה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רב holds אין זיקה, why didn't he simply say that the הלכה follows that opinion?
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him just say: the הלכה follows the one who says there is no זיקה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the way רב worded his ruling: a general statement would have been simpler.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether there is זיקה is an argument between תנאים. Instead of giving one specific case, רב could have just said which side the הלכה follows. The גמרא wants to know why he chose this particular wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (the תנא who holds this view)

phrases.english: So let him say:
the halacha follows the one who says there is no zikah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר אֵין זִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רב's ruling in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's choice to give a specific case instead of a general ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general ruling that the הלכה follows אין זיקה would be shorter and clearer.

steps.title: A general ruling might seem to cover only two brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a general ruling might have been limited to a case with two brothers, and we would think that with one brother there is זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had said that, I would have thought: that applies only when there are two brothers, but when there is one brother, there is זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב did not use the general wording: it could be misunderstood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there are two brothers, the widow is not tied to either one in particular, so the bond is weak. With only one brother, she is tied to him alone, so we might think the bond is real. רב's specific case teaches something the general wording would not.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only in this case)

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲוָה אָמַר הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא:
phrases.english: If he had said this, I would have said:
these words apply with two,
phrases.notes: Two brothers, each of whom could do יבום with her.

phrases.english: but with one, there is zikah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוָה אָמַר הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21's question about wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The general wording could be misread as limited
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אין זיקה would apply only when there are two brothers; with one brother there would be זיקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's ruling holds even with one brother, which the general wording would not make clear.

steps.title: Then why not say no זיקה even with one brother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: רב could have said the הלכה follows אין זיקה even with one brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him say: the הלכה follows the one who says there is no זיקה, even with one brother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks again: a general ruling that clearly includes one brother would solve the problem from step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22's worry was only that a general ruling might cover just two brothers. Adding 'even with one' fixes that. So why give a specific case at all?

phrases.english: So let him say: the halacha follows the one who says
there is no zikah even with one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר אֵין זִיקָה אֲפִילּוּ בְּחַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 22 and asks for an even clearer general wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's choice of a specific case, even after step 22's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'אין זיקה even with one' would cover the one-brother case without needing a specific case.

steps.title: Only after her death, not while she is alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a fully general ruling would suggest he may marry her mother even while the widow is alive. רב's case teaches it is allowed only after her death, because one may not cancel the מצוה of יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had said that, I would have thought he may marry her mother even while she is alive. So רב teaches us: after her death, yes; while she is alive, no, because it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final reason for רב's specific wording: it limits the permission to after the widow dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he married her mother while she was alive, the widow would become his wife's daughter and forbidden to him, so he could no longer do יבום. That cancels the מצוה, which is not allowed. Once she has died there is no מצוה left to cancel, so her mother is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: To cancel the מצוה of יבום

steps.whatToRemember: רב holds אין זיקה even with one brother, but he may marry the widow's mother only after she dies. While she is alive, he may not, because it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of יבום.
steps.confusionAlert: The reason he can't marry her mother while she is alive is NOT that there is זיקה. It is a separate reason: marrying the mother would cancel the מצוה of יבום.

phrases.english: If he had said this, I would have said:
even while she is alive,
so it teaches us
after death, yes; while alive, no,
because it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of yibum.
phrases.notes: Marrying her mother would make her his wife's daughter, who is forbidden to him, so he could no longer do יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמַר הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: אֲפִילּוּ מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 and explains why רב gave the specific case of a widow who died.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The general wording would be too broad
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A general ruling of אין זיקה would allow him to marry her mother even while the widow is alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: He may marry her mother only after the widow dies, because while she is alive it would cancel the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two separate reasons can forbid the same thing: זיקה, and the איסור of canceling יבום. Even someone who holds אין זיקה still has to deal with the second one.

steps.title: A משנה seems to permit only the sister, not the mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling from a משנה that permits the sister of a dead יבמה. This implies the mother is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: if his יבמה died, he is permitted to marry her sister. This implies: her sister, yes; her mother, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to challenge רב (step 20), who said the יבם may marry the mother of a שומרת יבם who died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only that the sister is permitted. If the mother were also permitted, the משנה should have said so. So it seems the mother is forbidden, which would mean יש זיקה, against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: His יבמה, the widow of his brother who is waiting for יבום
Her sister yes, her mother no. This is a reading drawn from exactly what the משנה says.

phrases.english: We learned: if his yevama died —
he is permitted to marry her sister.
Her sister, yes; her mother, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 20 using a משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the יבם may marry the mother of a שומרת יבם who died
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה permits only the sister. This implies the mother is forbidden, which fits יש זיקה.

steps.title: The wording was copied from the first part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The mother is really permitted too. The משנה only said 'sister' to match the wording of its first part, about a wife who died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even for her mother. But since the first part taught: if his wife died, he is permitted to her sister (her sister yes, but her mother no, because that is an איסור דאורייתא), the last part was also taught with the words 'permitted to her sister.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. It says the משנה's wording about the יבמה does not really mean to exclude the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first part, about a wife who died, saying 'sister' is exact: her mother stays forbidden forever by Torah law. The last part, about a יבמה, simply repeated the same wording, so we cannot learn from it that the mother is forbidden there.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because of (the wording used just before)
The first part of a משנה
The last part of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה is forbidding the mother in the case of a יבמה. The word 'sister' there is only borrowed from the first part, where the mother really is forbidden.

phrases.english: The same is true even for her mother,
but since it taught in the first part:
if his wife died — he is permitted to her sister,
her sister yes, but her mother no,
because she is a Torah prohibition —
phrases.notes: A man may never marry his wife's mother, even after his wife dies.

phrases.english: it also taught in the last part, 'permitted to her sister.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording borrowed for style (אַיְּידֵי), so it is not a precise inference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's mention of only the sister means the mother is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: The mother is permitted too. The word 'sister' just copies the first part's wording.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's view stands: after a שומרת יבם dies, her mother is permitted, because רב holds אין זיקה.

steps.title: רב יהודה forbids the mother, so he holds יש זיקה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules the opposite of רב: if a שומרת יבם dies, the יבם may not marry her mother. So he holds יש זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: if a שומרת יבם died, he is forbidden to marry her mother. Apparently he holds that there is a זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב יהודה's opposing ruling and draws the conclusion that he holds יש זיקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bond between the widow and the יבם is like a marriage (יש זיקה), her mother counts like a mother-in-law and stays forbidden even after the widow dies. This is the mirror image of רב in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for the יבם to do יבום or חליצה
The bond between the יבם and the widow counts like a marriage

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
a widow waiting for the yavam who died —
he is forbidden to marry her mother.
Apparently he holds there is a zikah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם שֶׁמֵּתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the opposite opinion to רב's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a שומרת יבם dies, the יבם may not marry her mother, because יש זיקה

steps.title: Why not simply rule like the view of יש זיקה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה gave a specific case instead of simply ruling like the opinion of יש זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him say: the הלכה follows the words of the one who says there is a זיקה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה used a roundabout case. The question matches the one asked about רב in step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב יהודה's whole point is יש זיקה, a short general ruling would have covered everything. Picking this particular case must teach something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה follows the words of

phrases.english: So let him say: the halacha follows the words of
the one who says there is a zikah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר יֵשׁ זִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way רב יהודה phrased his ruling in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The form of רב יהודה's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general ruling of יש זיקה would be shorter and clearer, so why give this specific case?

steps.title: A general ruling might be limited to one brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a general ruling would have been read as applying only when there is one brother, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had said that, I would have thought: this applies only with one brother, but with two brothers there is no זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer, similar to the one given for רב in step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one brother, the bond is strong because only he can do יבום. With two brothers, the bond is split between them and might seem weaker. So a general ruling might have been limited to one brother.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
These words apply (only in this case)

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲוָה אָמַר הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא:
phrases.english: If he had said that, I would have thought:
these words apply with one [brother],
but with two — there is no zikah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוָה אָמַר הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Prevents a mistaken narrow reading of a general ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A general 'יש זיקה' ruling would apply only to one brother
steps.terutzMaskana: A general ruling might be misread as limited to one brother, so רב יהודה gave a specific case instead. The next step rejects this answer.

steps.title: But the argument is about two brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer: the תנאים argue about זיקה in a case of two brothers, so ruling like יש זיקה would already cover two brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when they argue, don't they argue about a case of two brothers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer of step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original argument over זיקה is about a case with two brothers. Ruling like יש זיקה means ruling on that case itself, so no one could think it applies only to one brother.

phrases.english: But when they argue — don't they argue about two?
phrases.notes: 'They' are the תנאים who argue over whether there is זיקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'one brother vs. two' answer of step 29
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The argument itself is about two brothers, so a ruling like יש זיקה must include two brothers.

steps.title: Starting a new answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the first answer and begins a new one: 'If he had said this...'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if he had said this,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new answer to step 28. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the earlier answer is dropped. The new answer will explain what a general ruling would have gotten wrong, so רב יהודה needed his specific case.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the previous answer for a new one)

phrases.english: Rather: if he had said this,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 29 with a new answer, which is still being set up
steps.terutzResolutionType: New answer begins; its content continues in the next part of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A general ruling of יש זיקה would mislead in some way (explained next)
